title: Understanding the Objective Function
text: The objective function $R(\theta_1)$ is a sum of squared errors, but it's weighted by $x_i$. Think about how this affects the derivative.

title: Differentiation Step
text: When differentiating $R(\theta_1)$ with respect to $\theta_1$, consider the chain rule. The expression inside the sum is $(y_i-\theta_1x_i)**2$. What happens when you differentiate this with respect to $\theta_1$?

title: Applying the Chain Rule
text: Differentiate $(y_i-\theta_1x_i)**2$ with respect to $\theta_1$. What do you get?

title: Summation and Constants
text: Remember that when you differentiate a sum, you can differentiate each term individually. Also, the factor $1/n$ is a constant and can be factored out of the differentiation process.

title: Combining the Results
text: Combine the differentiated term with the constant factor $1/n$ and the summation. What is the derivative of $R(\theta_1)$?
